1

Details

Built by rerun/ntof/vt/make_vt_deck.py from the outputs of vt_table.py, vt_smooth.py and ab_compare.py (rerun/ntof/vt/README.md). Data: EOS Analysis_pass1/vt_table/.

v is measured from how long the charge column lasts, per acquisition and chamber

The fit never uses v; v only turns the fitted transverse speed w into an angle. Hover dotted terms and data points for details.

A track crossing the gap leaves charge at every depth; the strips see it arrive over the drift time of the full gap. Stacking many clean tracks and fitting the box edge gives T, independent of the angle.

B has no box (no field-shaping ring), so no v. D's beam column is not a box: D is measured on cosmic triggers only.

2

Details

Per (acquisition, arm): vt_acq.py (condor 4677358) keeps the pass's clean single tracks with one colsum cluster per view, and stores the strip-summed signals S (20 samples). vt_table.py drops saturated events and those with < 5 pulse strips, normalises each S to its maximum, fits the median stack with colsum.GridFit (T grid 5 ns), and bootstraps the error (60 resamples). v = gap/T per view, combined inverse-variance.

Caveats carried by the table: T is gain-confounded (+18 % across a det3 mesh scan) — irrelevant here, HV never changed in the campaign (A/B 540/700, C 525/700, D 520/700 V); beam and cosmic samples select different tracks, so the two trigger classes are kept apart; the 1.2 µs window can clip slow columns (C closest).

Sub-run pooled v from vt_table.py; smooth model vt_smooth.py (spline + water vapour).

3

Details

Model: ln v = c[arm, trigger] + s[arm]·g(t), with g one cubic P-spline (knots every 2 h, λ by block cross-validation) plus a water-vapour term; s_A = 1, fitted s_C = 3.08, s_D = 2.91. Levels (beam): A 39.68, C 30.30, D (cosmic) 34.55 µm/ns.

The chambers are in one gas line, A → B → C → D. Per sub-run correlations: A–C 0.85 (beam), C–D 0.68, A–D 0.57 (cosmic).

Chamber C: 27.7–32.0 µm/ns over the campaign

4

Details

Campaign median (beam, per sub-run): 30.60 µm/ns; the frozen bundle has 28.1. The bundle was calibrated on run_145 (5 Aug), the slowest part of the campaign, where the measured v is within 1 % of it (A 0.998, C 0.989): the bundles are right at their own run and the rest of the campaign is faster.

Cosmic triggers read about 1 % below beam on C (and 1.3 % above on A) within ±12 h: a selection difference, so each trigger class has its own level.

5

Details

A: campaign median 39.78 (beam), bundle 38.6 (+3.1 %).

D: 15–45 clean cosmic tracks per acquisition, so it is fitted per sub-run (238). Median 34.23 vs bundle 31.0: D reads ~+10 % even on its own calibration run (run_149), so D's absolute scale needs an angle anchor (gap error ±3.8 %, and its bundle v came from a different estimator). Its time dependence is what the model uses.

6

Details

Each point is one ~1 h sub-run measured in both chambers. The A–D and C–D clouds are wider because D has only 15–45 clean tracks per acquisition (error bars in the hover). The regression slopes are diluted by the noise on the x variable; the fitted chamber ratios are the model's s (C 3.0, D 2.9 relative to A).

7

Details

Within a ~1 h sub-run, acquisitions scatter by 0.41 µm/ns rms against a bootstrap error of 0.29, so v is smooth on the scale of hours; the model adds a jitter term per chamber (A 0.86 %, C 0.95 %) so that χ²/dof = 1. The gap at 29 Jul 13–19 h has no acquisitions: the band widens there.

Water vapour sets the trend, the hall temperature the daily wiggle

C's smooth v against MeteoSwiss Genève-Cointrin (UTC shifted to local time) and the ³He capsule gauge

8

Details

The 4–6 August dip in v sits on the campaign's most humid days (water vapour 20+ hPa). The daily cycle in v (fast around 06–07 h, slow 15–19 h) runs opposite to the capsule pressure, i.e. to the hall temperature. Outdoor air temperature and pressure track neither strongly.

Sources: MeteoSwiss open data ogd-smn_gve_t_recent.csv (station GVE, 10-min, UTC); the capsule log is the DAQ's he3_pressure watcher (Keithley 2000, P = (V − 1) × 400 bar), 5-min medians in ntof_run_report/data/he3_pressure_5min.csv. Cointrin is ~5 km from n_TOF.

Water vapour and hall temperature explain 78 % of C's variation

ln v = a + b·(outdoor water vapour, smoothed) + c·(capsule daily swing); C beam acquisitions

R²water %/hPahall %/K
A0.48-0.61-1.3
C0.78-1.88-2.2
D0.56-1.77-2.9

1 bar of capsule pressure ≈ 0.6 K of hall temperature (sealed volume, p ∝ T).

9

Details

Both signs are the wrong way for a gas-density (E/N) effect: at our field v would rise with temperature and fall with pressure. Instead v falls with both water and temperature, and by ~2 %/K on C, far more than density could give. The reading: water entering the gas (permeation through the lines, outgassing from the walls, both faster when warm and humid), more of it downstream in the A → B → C → D chain. This is a hypothesis from correlations with outdoor air; the gas itself was not measured.

τ = 24 h chosen by cross-validation of the water-only model (scan 8–48 h). Station pressure correlates +0.2–0.3 and outdoor temperature −0.3: both weaker.

68 % half-width of measured/model − 1. "water" = the water-vapour term alone, no spline: it gets most of the way, and the spline adds the rest. The random holdout (20 % of acquisitions) tests interpolation between neighbours; the block holdout tests a gap of 6 h.

Re-reconstructing with the measured v changes no fit, only which ~1 % of tracks are kept

A/B test: 30 beam acquisitions at the fastest times, frozen v (A) vs measured sub-run v (B)

A (v +3.5…5.1 %)C (v +12…15 %)

all tracks in both98.7 %99.1 %
tracks with |tan| < 0.5, A → B-0.6 %-0.2 %
chosen fits |tan| 0.5–0.6, A → B+9 %+46 %

The fit works in time units: w, p0, t0 are identical. Correcting tan in the tables gives what a rerun would.

v also sets the column-end window and the raw-tan edge used to rank candidates: that reshuffles ~1 % of tracks, counts within 0.6 %.

Decided 11-17: no rerun. Correct tan with v(t), cut |tan| < 0.5, state the ~1 % as a systematic.

11

Details

Bundles: the frozen A_E2_beam / C_E2_beam with only v_drift set to the sub-run's measured v (make_vt_ab.py, EOS Analysis_pass1/tests/vt_ab/); code ed0b1162, condor 4677861, 30/30 exit 0 on the first attempt. Comparison: ab_compare.py.

Before the jobs ran, a replay of the stored candidates (plausible = column end in the window and raw |tan| < 0.6, ranked by plausible then Δχ²) predicted the top-choice change on 4.7 % (A) and 3.8 % (C) of planes; observed 4.9 % and 3.9 %. Most of those are a reordering among tracks that are kept anyway: 98.7–99.1 % of all tracks are found in both.

These acquisitions are the campaign's extremes (C 12–15 % above the frozen v); typical acquisitions sit closer to it.

What this does not rule out, and what is next

Not ruled out

• The water reading is a correlation with outdoor air; the gas was never measured.

• D's absolute v reads ~10 % off its bundle even on its own run: its scale needs an angle anchor.

• A's shape is tied to C's (one curve): its own small departures (~0.9 %) are in its scatter.

• The A/B covers beam triggers of A and C; two-track splits were not separated.

Next

• Stage 3 on the desktop: tan_vt = tan × v_bundle / v(t) from the smooth model, per acquisition (or per event time).

• Acceptance |tan| < 0.5 in true angle, so it does not move with v.

• D's L1 beam re-run (condor 4677439) lands first; then the stage-3 rebuild for D.
